unit.title: Nuanced Subjunctive Triggers
unit.subtitle: El hecho de que, no es que, que yo sepa and value judgments

grammar.title: The subtle triggers natives never miss
grammar.intro: Beyond the obvious quiero / dudo / espero, C1 Spanish is full of quieter structures that quietly demand the subjunctive: fronted facts, denied causes, value judgments and a few fixed expressions. These are the ones that give away a non-native — learn to hear them and the mood becomes second nature.

sections.heading: El hecho de que + subjunctive
sections.body: When you comment on or react to a fact, el hecho de que takes the subjunctive — the fact is the topic, not fresh information. Native speakers do allow the indicative when they're purely asserting the fact as news, but the subjunctive is the safe, default choice after this phrase.

ex.es: El hecho de que llueva no cambia el plan.
ex.en: The fact that it's raining doesn't change the plan.

ex.es: El hecho de que llegues tarde molesta a todos.
ex.en: The fact that you arrive late annoys everyone.

sections.heading: No es que… (sino que) + subjunctive
sections.body: To deny a reason before giving the real one, use no es que + subjunctive, typically paired with sino que + indicative for the true explanation. The negated clause is hypothetical, so it stays in the subjunctive.

ex.es: No es que no me guste, sino que no tengo tiempo.
ex.en: It's not that I don't like it, it's that I don't have time.
ex.note: no es que + subj. / sino que + ind.

ex.es: No es que sea difícil, es que es aburrido.
ex.en: It's not that it's hard, it's that it's boring.

sections.heading: Value judgments + fixed expressions
sections.body: Impersonal value judgments — lo normal / lo lógico / lo raro es que and es una pena / lástima que — evaluate rather than report, so they take the subjunctive. The same holds for el que meaning “whoever” in a general sense.

ex.en: The logical thing is for you to apologize.

ex.es: El que lo sepa que levante la mano.
ex.en: Whoever knows it, raise your hand.

sections.heading: Que yo sepa / que yo recuerde
sections.body: These frozen hedges mean “as far as I know / recall” and are always in the subjunctive. They soften a claim, signalling the limits of your knowledge.

ex.en: As far as I know, nobody has resigned.
As far as I recall, he didn't say that.

takeaways: el hecho de que → subjunctive when you comment on the fact (the default at C1).
no es que + subjunctive denies a reason; the real one follows in sino que + indicative.
Value judgments — lo lógico/raro es que, es una pena que — take the subjunctive.
Fixed hedges que yo sepa / que yo recuerde are always subjunctive.

mistakes.w: No es que no me gusta, es que no puedo.
mistakes.r: No es que no me guste, es que no puedo.
mistakes.why: no es que denies a reason and requires the subjunctive: guste, not gusta.

mistakes.w: Que yo sé, nadie ha llamado.
mistakes.r: Que yo sepa, nadie ha llamado.
mistakes.why: The fixed hedge is que yo sepa (subjunctive), never que yo sé.

mistakes.w: Es una pena que no puedes venir.
mistakes.r: Es una pena que no puedas venir.
mistakes.why: A value judgment (es una pena que) triggers the subjunctive: puedas.

exercises.prompt: El hecho de que ___ tarde no justifica nada.
exercises.prompt_en: The fact that you arrive late justifies nothing.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! Comentar el hecho → el hecho de que + subjuntivo.
exercises.no: When you comment on the fact, “el hecho de que” takes the subjunctive: llegues.

exercises.prompt: No es que no ___, es que estoy agotado.
exercises.prompt_en: It's not that I don't want to, it's that I'm exhausted.
exercises.no: “No es que” denies a reason and needs the subjunctive: quiera.

exercises.prompt: Build: “It's a shame that you can't come.”
exercises.no: “Es una pena que no puedas venir” — the value judgment takes the subjunctive.

exercises.prompt: Que yo ___, nadie ha dicho semejante cosa. (recordar)
exercises.prompt_en: As far as I recall, nobody has said such a thing.
exercises.hint: The fixed hedge 'que yo…' is always subjunctive.
exercises.no: The frozen expression is “que yo recuerde”, in the subjunctive — not recuerdo.

exercises.prompt: Match each trigger to its English meaning.

exercises.tts: Lo lógico es que te disculpes.
accepted: lo logico es que te disculpes
exercises.translation: The logical thing is for you to apologize.
exercises.no: It was: “Lo lógico es que te disculpes.” (a value judgment → subjunctive).

exercises.scenario: A colleague asks about a pending decision 📋

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.es: ¿Sabes si han aprobado ya el proyecto?
lines.en: Do you know whether they've already approved the project?

options.text: Que yo sepa, todavía no lo han decidido.
Que yo sé, todavía no lo han decidido.
Que yo supiera, todavía no lo han decidido.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! “Que yo sepa” es la fórmula fija.
exercises.no: The fixed hedge is “que yo sepa” (present subjunctive), not sé or supiera.

exercises.say: No es que no me importe, es que no puedo.
exercises.en: It's not that I don't care, it's that I can't.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the rhythm of “No es que no me importe, es que no puedo.”
